description:
Combine the two latest gripper designs into one 3D project with four printable pieces.

Jake (voice): "Can you make sure GPT-6 [transcribed 'gpt six astro'] is working on this. And then I want you to try to combine those most recent pebbles into a single 3D project that has all four pieces: the left and right of one gripper, and the left and right of the other. Take good ideas from each one and come up with something that's easy to 3D print and will work really well for collecting demonstration data that we can then give to the robot. And we should also be able to adapt it to the SO-101 arms. Combine from those two ideas and come up with something that's really simple, does what we need, has easy ways to grip, and feels really natural in the human hand."

Sources (read both, including their latest agent results):
- voice-6d8b9fd8 (pebbles/human): simplified Generalist-style handheld gripper. Latest build (2026-10-14, commit after 466c992): hub + two yellow geared jaws (mirror via gear sectors, 56 mm gape) + camera bracket on the hub looking down the jaws; finger sleeve (index+middle) and thumb sleeve on the OUTER faces of the jaws, behind the gripping face ("pinching paper"); one extra arm-only cradle for the SO-101 gripper servo on the stock wrist mount. CAD: cad/openscad/hand_gripper/ (hand_gripper.scad, build.sh, export/parts.json, render/). Open guesses: servo size, hub pressing the thumb web on small hands.
- voice-805d4970 (pebbles/human): New Caledonian crow beak gripper. Latest build (2026-10-14): you hold the beak directly; thumb dent on top jaw (24x15x2.5 mm), index+middle along the bottom jaw, two strap loops per jaw for a 20 mm velcro strap so you can pull it open as well as squeeze; five prints: top jaw/body, bottom (moving) jaw, pivot plug (M3 hinge in place of the servo for handheld), camera mount, wrist puck (SO-101 adapter on the stock horn pattern, dovetail dock). CAD: cad/openscad/crow/ (crow_hand.scad, crow_upper/lower/beak/dock.scad, check_interference.sh, check_budget.py, export/parts.json), plan in plans/crow_gripper.md. Capture plan defers to voice-b4fbc4ee.

Spec:
- ONE 3D project/view (same app viewer, assembled/exploded toggle) showing four printable jaw pieces: left + right jaw of design A (Generalist-style) and left + right jaw of design B (crow beak), plus whatever shared parts they need (hub/pivot, camera mount, SO-101 adapter).
- Merge the best ideas: natural handheld grip with finger and thumb on the outside of the jaws, thumb indent, strap loops so the jaws can be pulled open; camera mount that sees the jaw tips from the same spot in hand and on the arm (UMI-style demo collection).
- One shared SO-101 mount/adapter so the same jaws go on the arm.
- Simple and easy to print: few parts, no supports where possible, every moving part a separate piece.
- Attach renders (assembled, exploded, in-hand) to the reply. Don't claim it grips well or transfers data until printed and tested.

Model: Jake asked for GPT-6 to work this; dispatch_target is set to codex / gpt-6-astra.

results.identified_issue:
Worked only voice-427220cb. Read both requested source conversations and their latest results. New cad/openscad/demo_gripper is an additive unified project; prior designs and their pebbles are untouched. Its four jaws are genuinely interchangeable on one 24 mm pitch-spacing geared hub, not the old incompatible mechanisms arranged together. A borrows the broad Generalist-like pinch, B the taper, opposing V seats and one gated recess. B deliberately changes from a fixed upper mandible to symmetric actuation and is a new tool/calibration ID. Both have an outside 2.5 mm saddle, a 22x3 mm through-slot for 20 mm straps, wider index/middle contact, and flat Y=-5 bed surfaces. Not sized for four fingers. Bare faces close to 0.8 mm gap; approximately 0.5 mm compliant tape per face is required for a paper trial and changes calibration.

Reuse the old hub, servo cradle, stop tabs and gear geometry through OpenSCAD use; do not duplicate their owner. Mesh connectivity tests exposed detached half-phase teeth caused by the faceted original root radius. This project adds a 10.35 mm sector root to bond the teeth and validates single-solid exports plus engagement/clearance. This does NOT patch the old project. Added keyed handheld insert supports the driven pivot through the horn port; remove insert and driven M3 pivot for the servo. The camera bracket is new: old optical center (0,44,-34) hid open tips; new (0,65,20) aims at (0,0,60), retains 32 mm board/28 mm M2 square. Ray tests cover tips at 0/14/29.5 deg for A/B, with bare assembly, schematic hand/straps, and arm with assumed servo envelope. 36 clear rays; max off-axis 28.04 deg against an assumed 70-degree usable field in BOTH image axes. Real hand/objects/wiring and actual lens remain untested.

export.py generates only CAD assets (no app build/install/deploy), eight app-position STLs and parts.json, four print-position jaw STLs in jaws_print_ready.zip, five renders. A sits on hub, B pair is offset +140 mm, arm-only cradle parked at Y=-85 so mutually exclusive insert/cradle are not overlapped. Existing viewer loads the kit generically; existing designs remain historical entries. validate.py verifies 8 watertight consistently-wound single connected meshes, 4 Z=0 bed-contact exports, 70 motion/fit/gear/stop cases (including positive controls), and existing stager discovery/8 parts. Results committed as validation.json and camera_check.txt. No app/device run and no build. Shared hub/horn and angled camera can require support; only jaw prints are specifically laid out for no designed supports.

SO-101 wrist pattern inherited from source CAD; servo 45.2x24.7x35 envelope, shaft/horn stack and screw positions still guesses. No measured fit, load, payload, comfort or transfer claim. README supplies assembly/print guidance and a capture contract referencing existing plans/handheld_gripper.md. Removing phone/trigger leaves pose and jaw sensing unsolved; no capture software added and unpowered servo back-drive is not assumed acceptable. Preserve physical camera/extrinsics between modes, identify A/B separately, measure jaw angle and pose with timestamps, recalibrate arm limits, then run a matched hand/arm pilot. Render hand/straps are schematic, not anthropometric evidence.
results.summary: Combined both grippers into one eight-piece kit with four interchangeable jaws and a shared camera and SO-101 mount.
results.detailed_description:
Yellow is the broad pinch pair; teal is the crow-inspired pair with rod notches and a gated recess. Both use outside thumb/finger rests and strap slots. The crow jaws now move symmetrically to fit the same hub. Four jaw STLs are supplied flat for printing; some shared parts still need supports.

I moved the camera forward so open jaws no longer hide their tips in the CAD checks. The project uses the existing Assemble/Explode viewer, with the spare pair alongside. Assembled, exploded and both in-hand renders are attached.

Eight solid meshes, 70 motion/fit checks and 36 camera sightlines passed. Nothing has been printed or tested in the app; servo dimensions remain assumptions, and recording still needs pose and jaw-angle sensing. Print one jaw pair and the handheld hub/insert first to check fit.

summary: Merge the Generalist-style hand gripper and the crow beak gripper into one 3D project with four printable jaw pieces, left and right of each, plus shared hub, camera mount, and SO-101 adapter. Keep outside finger and thumb grips, thumb indent, and strap loops, with one camera view and one arm mount, simple supportless prints, and assembled, exploded, and in-hand renders without claiming it grips well until tested.
